_comment: Combat rules and MONSTER data. Frame counts are simulation ticks (60 per second). Numbers are placeholders to tune by feel. MONSTER STRENGTH is meant to track the player: level-1 monsters are balanced against the starter gear (about ATK 13.5, DEF 92, HP 112; HP SCALE 100 since 2026-11-13: every HP and ATK number in data, players and monsters alike, was divided by 10 so a starter card shows 100 HP; DEF stays because the DEF rule DEF/(DEF+defense_constant) has no HP unit): a grunt dies in about 3 combos, a charger in about 5, a brute in about 11 heavy hits, and a monster light hit takes about 4-6% of the player's HP, a heavy or slam about 11-16%. enemy_level_scaling = how much a monster grows per level above 1, so a stage for better gear just sets a higher level on its spawns (map enemy_spawns[].level). The player's weapons (fists, sword, dagger, spear, hammer and their moves) are in weapons.json. A move chains into on_light / on_heavy when that button was pressed during the move and the active frames are over. invuln_from/invuln_to (inclusive/exclusive, in move frames) make the fighter untouchable during that part of the move. telegraph = the client warns the player during the wind-up. advance = forward rush speed during the swing.
_coop_comment: M2 prototype, enabled only for explicit 2-4 player sessions. ADR HP scaling; revive/bleedout values are initial test tuning pending playtest. Stand still near a downed ally to revive; no extra button/codec bit is needed.
_ranged_comment: RANGED ATTACKS (logic/projectiles.gd). A move fires through its 'spawns' list: {projectile: id | area: id | blink: meters, frame: move frame (default = its startup, the strike), offset: [forward, up, side (+ = the shooter's right)] from the feet in meters, measured on the clip's release frame (2026-10-12: archer arrow tip at frame 34 of shoot / 44 of volley, mage crystal at frame 30 of cast, where the staff has thrust forward), angle: degrees off the facing}. A move with spawns hits only through them (melee: true to also swing). Damage, guard, dodge and effects are the melee rules with the move's power. PROJECTILES: look = how the client draws it (arrow, bolt), speed m/s, range m it flies, radius m, pierce = extra targets it passes through, gravity m/s2 down and lift = m/s up at release (an arrow's slight arc), homing = degrees per second it turns toward its target (0 = none, weak = 30-60), walls = stops at walls and the floor, aim_cone = it aims straight at the nearest opponent within this many degrees of the facing (free aim; otherwise straight ahead). It can be guarded from the front (unless the move ignores_guard) and i-frames let it fly through. AREAS: a circle marked on the ground at the opponent the caster faces (within range and aim_cone), radius m, delay = ticks of warning before it goes off (at least 20; the circle fills up meanwhile), active = ticks it hurts (each opponent once), height m it reaches up, guardable (false: step out or dodge).
_goblin_comment: The goblin's own twin-dagger moves (not the player's dagger set), timed to the animator's clips (art/animations/goblin.json): goblin_jab = attack_1 (marks 0.20/0.43/0.90 s; 10/4/16 frames, so the clip plays about 1.8x fast), goblin_lunge = attack_2 (marks 0.60/0.92/1.80 s; 30/10/34 frames = 0.5 s telegraphed wind-up). Both move only as the clips do (advance 0, Boss 2026-10-10: a realistic lunge): the lunge's hit box sits 0.3 m further out to match the clip's pounce, so it lands from the same striking spot as the jab. body_height 0.98 = it is hit only where its body is. flee_hp/flee_ticks: below 30% health it runs away for 1.25 s, once, then comes back. The Goblin Chief (the journey boss) is the same model and clips 1.3x bigger and darker (model_tint), with its own moves scaled to its reach. MOVESPD -12 (3.3 m/s) keeps the run clip's feet planted (authored for 2.44 m/s, played 0.6-1.4x).
_monster_comment: A monster may use any weapon style from weapons.json (the grunt uses fists, so it also has the fists skill: it sometimes works itself into a Rage). Monster stamina is only used by that skill. skill_chance (percent) = how often its AI uses the style's special skill instead of its normal attack. Monsters' buffs and debuffs are the same effects the player uses (effects.json); EFFECT_RES makes a monster hard to stun, shock or poison. model (optional) = a .glb facing +Z, feet at the bottom; it is scaled so its full bounds (hats, horns, crowns included) are model_height meters, while body_height is the body the rules hit; an untextured model is tinted like the capsule (state colors), a textured one keeps its texture and the state tints multiply it; without one the monster is a capsule. animations (optional) = its animation set .glb (idle, run, attack_1, attack_2, hit, death + a .json of windup_end/strike_end/length marks next to it); if that file is missing the model's own clips are used, and with none the model is static. clips = which clip each of its moves plays (default attack_1); standin_clips (optional) = what to play while the set does not have that clip yet (every goblin variant has its own clips since 2026-10-12). nock_mesh = a mesh of the model shown only while a firing move winds up (the archer's arrow on the string). ai.retreat_ticks = after each attack it backs off from the player this long (hit and run).

mummy.role: Mummy: regular melee undead. Core combat stats and movement/attack speed tuned to1.5x the normal Goblin baseline; unarmed strikes, no retreat or ranged skill.
mummy._design: Boss2026-10-21: base combat stats1.5x normal Goblin at the same level. HP450/ATK150/DEF45;MOVESPD32 gives1.32x base walk versus Goblin0.88x (=1.5x). ATKSPD50 gives1.5x move-frame speed;AI cooldowns40–73ticks from Goblin60–110 divided by1.5 (integer rounding). Zero CRIRATE/poise stay zero. Fists moves remain provisional; exact hit damage/DPS also depends on move power,timing and target DEF. Rig1.80m,bespoke clips and separate map pending.

dummy_grunt.role: Grunt: walks up and jabs. Beat it with combos.

brute.role: Brute: slow, tough, raises its arms before a huge slam. DODGE the slam.

charger.role: Charger: crouches, then rushes in a straight line. GUARD it or step out of the lane.

goblin.role: Goblin: small, twitchy, comes in packs. Darts in, stabs, hops back; glows before a leaping lunge. Catch it as it lands.

goblin_chief.role: Goblin Chief: crowned, nearly twice a goblin's size, twin cleavers. It stands its ground: a quick chop and a telegraphed leaping lunge with long reach; it shrugs off light hits. DODGE the lunge.

goblin_archer.role: Goblin Archer: hangs back and shoots. It draws before each arrow (no '!': only the 3-arrow volley warns, Boss 2026-10-10); sidestep or guard it, then close in: it backs away but cannot fight up close.

goblin_mage.role: Goblin Mage: keeps away, throws slow homing bolts and marks the ground where you stand: the circle fills, then bursts. Keep moving; it blinks away when you reach it.

goblin_knight.role: Goblin Knight: slow, armored, a greatsword taller than itself held ONE-HANDED (the goblin's fists can never meet on one hilt; the off-hand swings free). It never retreats or flees: a heavy, deliberate advance that closes the distance by never backing off, poise 140 so light hits do not stagger it. Each swing is wound up a long time ('!'): the side cleave, and an overhead that steps forward as it falls (advance) so it still catches a player who stands still. Dodge through a swing or step back, then hit it while it recovers.
goblin_knight._design: One-handed grip is what the animator's clips do now (tools/blender/goblin_family_clips.py: 'one hilt, so the greatsword is swung one-handed, grip_offhand stays unused'); the run clip is already a heavy armoured stomp with the blade dragged behind. No skeleton/arm change. No two-hand assumptions live in data: move ids (cleave/overhead) and VFX keys (vfx.json windup/swing/<move>) are grip-neutral. SPEED: MOVESPD -48 => 3.8 * 0.52 = 1.98 m/s, about 59% of a goblin's 3.34 m/s (goblin MOVESPD -12). run_clip_speed 1.55: the client plays the walk clip at speed / (run_clip_speed * model_fit); knight model_fit ~= 1.28, so 1.55 * 1.28 = 1.98 m/s reference => the heavy stomp plays at ~1.0x (its authored deliberate cadence) at the knight's own slow speed, instead of being pinned near the 0.6x clamp floor of the shared 2.44 reference (which caps how slow a monster can be shown).
